Santos, HR Manager DATE: June 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Guidelines for Intern Records In line with the Cooperative's commitment to proper documentation, transparency, and efficient personnel management, all departments are hereby directed to strictly observe the standard guidelines in maintaining and handling intern records. Completion Requirements Interns must complete all required documents, including clearance forms and final reports, prior to issuance of the Certificate of Completion. The Human Resource Unit shall monitor compliance with these guidelines. Any discrepancies or incomplete submissions shall be addressed accordingly. All concerned are enjoined to observe strict compliance with this Memorandum. MARIA L. SANTOS HR Manager Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative

PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte MEMORANDUM NO. 21 Series of 2026 TO: All Cooperative Officers, Department Heads, Staff, Interns, and Members FROM: Atty. Roberto C. Fernandez, Compliance Officer DATE: March 10, 2026 SUBJECT: Update on Data Privacy and Confidentiality of Member and Personnel Records In compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173) and the Cooperative's commitment to protecting personal information, this Memorandum serves to notify all concerned of the revised privacy protocols effective April 1, 2026. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte MEMORANDUM NO. 203 Series of 2026 TO: All Department Heads, Supervisors, Staff, and Interns FROM: Maria L. Santos, HR Manager DATE: July 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Incident Report Protocol for Workplace Accidents, Misconduct, and Security Breaches In line with the Cooperative's commitment to maintaining a safe, secure, and disciplined work environment, this Memorandum establishes the official protocol for reporting and documenting any workplace incident, including but not limited to accidents, injuries, property damage, misconduct, data breaches, or security threats. All personnel and interns are required to familiarize themselves with the following procedures. Strict compliance is mandatory. I. Definition of Reportable Incident Any unplanned event that results in or has the potential to result in: Physical injury to any person (employee, intern, member, or visitor) Damage to cooperative property or assets Violation of cooperative policies (e.g., harassment, theft, negligence) Data privacy or security breach Near-miss events (no injury but high risk) II. Reporting Procedures A. Immediate Response (Within 1 hour of incident) 1. Ensure safety of all individuals involved. Provide first aid or call emergency services if needed. 2. Secure the area and preserve evidence (photos, CCTV, physical objects). 3. Notify the immediate supervisor and the HR Unit verbally or via phone. B. Written Incident Report (Within 24 hours) The involved person or the first responsible officer must complete the standard Incident Report Form (attached) containing: Date, time, and exact location of incident Names and roles of persons involved and witnesses Detailed narrative (what happened, how, why, equipment used) Type of injury or damage (if any) Immediate action taken C. Submission and Routing Submit the accomplished Incident Report Form to the HR Unit via email (hr@panabomultipurpose.coop) or hard copy to HR Office. HR shall log the report and assign an Incident Reference Number (format: INC-YYYY-XXXX). HR forwards copies to the Compliance Officer and General Manager within 48 hours. III. Investigation and Resolution The HR Unit, together with the Compliance Officer, shall conduct an investigation within five (5) working days. Findings and recommendations shall be issued in a written Incident Investigation Report. Corrective actions may include: additional training, policy revisions, disciplinary action (verbal warning, suspension, termination), or repair/replacement of assets. IV. Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation All incident reports shall be treated as confidential documents accessible only to authorized personnel. Retaliation against any person who reports an incident in good faith is strictly prohibited and will result in disciplinary action. V. Penalties for Non-Compliance Failure to report a known incident within 24 hours, or knowingly submitting false information, shall be considered a serious violation and may result in suspension or termination of employment/internship. VI. Attachments Appendix A: Incident Report Form (to be printed and accomplished) Appendix B: Emergency Contact Numbers -- Panabo City This Memorandum takes effect immediately upon issuance. All previous incident reporting guidelines are hereby superseded. For clarifications, please contact the HR Unit at local 203 or email hr@panabomultipurpose.coop. MARIA L. SANTOS HR Manager Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative Noted by: ROBERTO V. TAN General Manager

PREFACE AND SCOPE This Human Resources Policy Manual (the 'Manual') sets forth the official policies, standards, and procedures governing personnel management at Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC). It applies to all regular, contractual, probationary, project-based employees, and interns. All personnel are required to read, understand, and comply with the provisions herein. Any violation may result in disciplinary action. 2. RECRUITMENT AND SELECTION 2.1 Staffing requests must be submitted by Department Heads to HR at least 30 days before the intended start date. 2.2 Job postings shall be published internally for 5 working days before external advertising. 2.3 Selection process includes: Initial screening and qualifications review Written examination (if applicable) Panel interview with at least three (3) interviewers Background and character reference check 2.4 For intern applicants, requirements include: Endorsement letter from school Updated resume Signed Internship Agreement (coop-school-intern) 3. EMPLOYMENT CLASSIFICATION Type Regular Probationary Period 6 months Conversion Criteria Satisfactory performance rating plus no major infraction Type Probationary Probationary Period 6 months renewable once Conversion Criteria Must meet KPIs and attendance requirement (≥95%) Type Project-based Probationary Period None (co-terminus with project) Conversion Criteria Not applicable Type Casual Probationary Period 3 months Conversion Criteria If assigned permanent function, may be regularized Type Intern Probationary Period None Conversion Criteria Completion of required hours and final report [Page 3] 4. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS 4.1 Salaries are released every 15th and 30th/31st of the month via payroll bank transfer. 4.2 Minimum wage for rank-and-file: ₱425.00 per day (as of 2026, per DOLE Region XI). Cooperative employees receive an additional ₱25.00 hardship allowance. 4.3 Mandatory benefits (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) are remitted by PCMC. 4.4 Cooperative-specific benefits: Year-end cash gift (₱5,000 for regular employees) Rice subsidy (10 kg per month) Free annual medical check-up at Panabo City Health Office Loyalty bonus (₱2,000 per year of service after 5 years) 4.5 Interns receive a transportation allowance of ₱100 per day attended. 5. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVE POLICIES 5.1 Official working hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (lunch break 12:00 NN – 1:00 PM). Some departments observe shifting schedules. 5.2 Tardiness beyond 15 minutes is recorded as late. Three (3) lates in one month = 1 day unpaid deduction. 5.3 Leave entitlements (regular employees): Leave Type Vacation Leave Number of Days 15 days/year Conditions With pay, unused up to 10 days carry over Leave Type Sick Leave Number of Days 15 days/year Conditions Medical certificate required for >3 consecutive days Leave Type Emergency Leave Number of Days 5 days/year Conditions For death of immediate family or calamity Leave Type Maternity Leave Number of Days 105 days Conditions Full pay per R.A. 11210 Leave Type Paternity Leave Number of Days 7 days Conditions Full pay Leave Type Parental Leave for Solo Parents Number of Days 7 days/year Conditions Full pay Leave Type Special Leave for Women Number of Days 2 days/month Conditions Gynecological conditions 5.4 Interns are entitled to emergency leave without pay but may coordinate with their school supervisor for excused absences. [Page 4] 6. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE The following are prohibited and subject to disciplinary action: 6.1 Light Offenses (1st offense: verbal warning; 2nd: written reprimand; 3rd: 1-day suspension) Unexcused tardiness or early departure Improper dress/uniform violation Use of mobile phone during work hours without permission Failure to log attendance 6.2 Grave Offenses (1st offense: 15-day suspension; 2nd: termination) Theft or misappropriation of cooperative funds or property Dishonesty or falsification of documents Harassment (sexual, verbal, or physical) Being under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs during work hours Gross negligence resulting in damage to coop assets 6.3 All disciplinary actions require an Investigation Report signed by HR Manager and Employee/Intern. 7. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION 7.1 Regular employees undergo semi-annual evaluation (June and December). 7.2 Interns are evaluated monthly by their assigned supervisor using the standard Intern Evaluation Form (attached as Annex C). 7.3 Rating scale: Rating 5 – Excellent Description Exceeds expectations Action Promotion eligible / bonus Rating 4 – Very Satisfactory Description Consistently meets Action Regularization if probationary Rating 3 – Satisfactory Description Meets minimum Action No action Rating 2 – Needs Improvement Description Below standard Action Performance improvement plan Rating 1 – Unsatisfactory Description Fails to meet Action Termination or non-renewal [Page 5] 8. TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT 8.1 Each employee is required to complete at least 16 hours of training per year. 8.2 Interns must complete the mandatory orientation on Day 1 and any department-specific training. 8.3 Training records are maintained by HR. Non completion without valid reason may affect performance rating. 9. HEALTH, SAFETY, AND WELFARE 9.1 PCMC maintains a Clinic at the ground floor with a part time nurse every Tuesday and Thursday. 9.2 Fire and earthquake drills are conducted quarterly. 9.3 All workplace accidents must be reported using the Incident Report Form (see Memorandum No. 203). 9.4 Interns are covered by the Cooperative's accident insurance while on duty. 10. INTERNSHIP PROGRAM POLICIES 10.1 Minimum internship duration: 250 hours. 10.2 Interns must submit: Intern Information Sheet (Day 1) Signed Confidentiality Agreement Weekly Accomplishment Report (every Friday) Final Report and Clearance (last day) 10.3 Interns are not allowed to operate cash or sign financial documents alone. 10.4 Certificate of Completion is issued only after HR verifies all required documents. 11. DATA PRIVACY AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT 11.1 Personnel files are stored in a locked cabinet accessible only to HR staff. 11.2 Digital records are password-protected with access logs. 11.3 Employee records are retained for 5 years after separation; intern records for 2 years. 11.4 Any breach must be reported per Memorandum No. 21 (Privacy Update). [Page 6] 12. GRIEVANCE MECHANISM Step 1 – The employee/intern discusses the concern with the immediate supervisor. Step 2 – If unresolved, a written grievance is filed with HR on the prescribed form. HR acknowledges within 24 hours. Step 3 – HR Manager and Compliance Officer conduct a hearing within 5 working days. Step 4 – Resolution is issued within 10 working days from filing. Step 5 – Appeal to the General Manager within 5 working days from resolution. GM’s decision is final. 13. SEPARATION AND CLEARANCE 13.1 A resigning employee must submit a resignation letter at least 30 days in advance. 13.2 Completion of Clearance Form is required to release final pay and Certificate of Employment. 13.3 Interns must complete the Intern Clearance Form and return all issued IDs and equipment. 14. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte CODE OF CONDUCT FOR EMPLOYEES AND INTERNS Document Code: PCMC-HR-COD-2026 Effective Date: March 1, 2026 Version: 2.0 Approved by: General Manager PREAMBLE This Code of Conduct sets forth the standards of behavior, ethics, and professionalism expected from all employees (regular, probationary, casual, project based) and interns of the Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC). It applies during work hours, cooperative sponsored events, and any other setting where the individual represents the cooperative. All personnel must read, understand, and strictly adhere to this Code. Violations shall result in disciplinary actions as outlined herein. TABLE OF CONTENTS 1. CORE VALUES 2. GENERAL CONDUCT STANDARDS 3. SPECIFIC RULES FOR EMPLOYEES 4. SPECIFIC RULES FOR INTERNS 5. PROHIBITED ACTS AND OFFENSES 6. DISCIPLINARY PENALTIES 7. REPORTING VIOLATIONS 8. ACKNOWLEDGMENT FORM 1. CORE VALUES All employees and interns shall uphold the cooperative's core values: Integrity Act honestly, transparently, and with accountability. Service Excellence Deliver quality service to members, clients, and the public. Teamwork Collaborate respectfully with all personnel. Professionalism Maintain proper demeanor, appearance, and work ethic. Stewardship Protect cooperative assets, funds, and confidential information. 2. GENERAL CONDUCT STANDARDS 2.1 Punctuality and Attendance All personnel must observe official working hours (8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday). Tardiness beyond 15 minutes requires a written explanation. 2.2 Proper Attire Employees must wear the prescribed cooperative uniform with ID on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. Business casual is allowed on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Interns must wear their internship ID and appropriate business attire unless a uniform is provided. 2.3 Respect in the Workplace Harassment, bullying, discrimination, or any form of verbal, physical, or sexual abuse is strictly prohibited. 2.4 Confidentiality Personnel files, member data, financial records, and internal memos shall not be disclosed to unauthorized persons. 2.5 Use of Cooperative Property Computers, phones, vehicles, and equipment are for work related purposes only. Personal use must be limited and with permission. 2.6 Conflict of Interest Personnel shall not engage in outside work or business that competes with the cooperative or uses cooperative resources for personal gain. 3. SPECIFIC RULES FOR EMPLOYEES Rule 3.1 Employees must report any change in personal information (address, contact number, civil status) to HR within 10 working days. Rule 3.2 Overtime must be pre approved by the Department Head and logged in the Overtime Form. Rule 3.3 Personal calls and text messages during work hours should be limited to emergencies. Rule 3.4 Employees are prohibited from accepting gifts, loans, or favors from coop members or suppliers that may influence decision making. Rule 3.5 Alcohol and illegal drugs are forbidden on cooperative premises. Smoking is allowed only in designated areas. Rule 3.6 Social media posts that damage the cooperative's reputation or disclose internal matters are prohibited. 4. SPECIFIC RULES FOR INTERNS Rule 4.1 Interns must comply with all general conduct standards applicable to employees. Rule 4.2 Interns shall not handle cash, sign checks, or approve financial transactions alone. A supervisor must be present. Rule 4.3 Weekly Accomplishment Reports must be submitted every Friday to the HR Unit. Rule 4.4 Interns are required to complete the mandatory orientation and any training assigned by their supervisor. Rule 4.5 Absences must be reported to the assigned supervisor and the HR Unit at least one hour before the start of shift. Rule 4.6 Interns shall not access confidential member or personnel data without specific authorization. Rule 4.7 Upon completion of the internship, all issued items (ID, uniform, keys, etc.) must be returned before the Certificate of Completion is released. 5. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte WORKPLACE SAFETY HANDBOOK Revision 2 Document Code: PCMC-HSE-HB-2026-002 Effective Date: April 1, 2026 Previous Revision: January 15, 2024 Approved by: General Manager FOREWORD This Workplace Safety Handbook is issued to all employees, interns, and regular visitors of Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC). It outlines the cooperative's commitment to providing a safe and healthy work environment in compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Standards (OSHS) of the Philippines (Department Order No. 198, series of 2018) and the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) guidelines. All personnel are required to read, understand, and follow the safety rules and emergency procedures contained in this handbook. A copy shall be kept in every department and made available to all staff. TABLE OF CONTENTS 1. GENERAL SAFETY POLICY 2. RESPONSIBILITIES 3. HOUSEKEEPING AND WORKPLACE ORDER 4. PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) 5. OFFICE AND COMPUTER SAFETY 6. FIRE SAFETY AND EVACUATION 7. EARTHQUAKE AND OTHER NATURAL DISASTERS 8. FIRST AID AND MEDICAL EMERGENCIES 9. REPORTING ACCIDENTS AND NEAR MISSES 10. CHEMICAL AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS 11. SAFETY SIGNS AND LABELS 12. EMERGENCY CONTACTS 13. ACKNOWLEDGMENT FORM 1. GENERAL SAFETY POLICY PCMC is committed to: Providing a workplace free from recognized hazards. Complying with all applicable safety and health laws. Investigating all accidents and implementing corrective actions. Training all personnel on emergency procedures. Encouraging active participation in safety programs. Violation of safety rules may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination or termination of internship. 2. RESPONSIBILITIES 2.1 Management Provide adequate safety equipment and training. Conduct regular safety inspections (monthly). Appoint Safety Officers (see Section 12). 2.2 Supervisors Enforce safety rules in their areas. Correct unsafe conditions immediately. Report all incidents to HR and Safety Officer. 2.3 Employees and Interns Follow all safety rules. Report hazards, accidents, or near misses to the supervisor. Use required PPE where applicable. Attend safety drills and training sessions. 3. HOUSEKEEPING AND WORKPLACE ORDER Keep aisles, exits, and stairways clear of obstructions at all times. Store boxes, files, and supplies on shelves not on the floor. Clean up spills immediately. Use wet floor signs. Dispose of trash in proper bins. Separate hazardous waste (batteries, toners, chemicals). Do not block fire extinguishers, electrical panels, or emergency exits. Maintain clear visibility of safety signs. 4. PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) Area or Task General office, Required PPE Closed shoes, ID, When All times. Cashier or Teller, None additional, During cash handling. Maintenance or Repair, Safety goggles, gloves, hard hat (if working at height), As assigned. Cleaning with chemicals, Rubber gloves, mask, When using bleach or solvents. Any emergency evacuation, None; follow exit signs, During drills or actual emergencies. PPE is provided by the cooperative. Report damaged or missing PPE to your supervisor. 5. OFFICE AND COMPUTER SAFETY Arrange workstations to avoid tripping over cables. Use cable ties or floor covers. Do not overload electrical outlets. Use surge protectors. Adjust chair and monitor height to prevent ergonomic strain. Take 5 minute breaks every hour. Do not place hot drinks near computers or documents. Report frayed wires, broken chairs, or loose railings to the Maintenance Unit. 6. FIRE SAFETY AND EVACUATION 6.1 Fire Prevention Smoking is allowed only in the designated smoking area (outside the building, away from gas tanks). Unplug non essential equipment at the end of the day. Do not store flammable liquids inside offices. 6.2 In Case of Fire Activate the nearest fire alarm (pull station). Call the Fire Marshall or Emergency Hotline (see Section 12). Use a fire extinguisher only if you are trained and the fire is small. Evacuate immediately via the nearest exit. Do not use elevators. 6.3 Evacuation Procedures Follow the posted evacuation map (located near all exits). Proceed to the designated assembly point: Cooperative Parking Lot, West Side. Wait for headcount. Report missing persons to the Safety Officer. Do not re enter the building until declared safe. 6.4 Fire Drills Fire drills are conducted quarterly (March, June, September, December). Participation is mandatory for all personnel and interns. 7. EARTHQUAKE AND OTHER NATURAL DISASTERS 7.1 During an Earthquake (Indoors) DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON. Get under a sturdy desk or table. Stay away from windows, cabinets, and hanging objects. 7.2 During an Earthquake (Outdoors) Move to an open area away from buildings, trees, and power lines. 7.3 After Shaking Stops Evacuate to the assembly point (Parking Lot, West Side). Do not use elevators. Check for injuries. 7.4 Typhoon and Flood Monitor weather updates via PAGASA. If signal No. 3 or above is raised in Davao del Norte, non essential personnel may be dismissed early. Do not cross flooded streets. Wait for clearance. 8. FIRST AID AND MEDICAL EMERGENCIES First aid kits are located in: HR Unit (Ground Floor), Cashier's Area (First Floor), Maintenance Shed, Interns' Work Area (Human Resource Unit). For minor injuries (small cuts, burns), use the first aid kit and report to your supervisor. For serious injuries (unconsciousness, heavy bleeding, difficulty breathing): 1. Call nearest first aider or Safety Officer. 2. Do not move the victim unless in immediate danger. 3. Call emergency services: Panabo City Rescue Unit 0917-111-2222 (see Section 12). Clinic nurse is available every Tuesday and Thursday, 9:00 AM to 12:00 NN at the Ground Floor Clinic. 9. REPORTING ACCIDENTS AND NEAR MISSES All accidents, injuries, and near misses (incidents that could have caused injury) must be reported using the Incident Report Form (see Memorandum No. 203). Report to immediate supervisor within 1 hour. Submit written report to HR within 24 hours. HR will investigate and implement corrective measures. Failure to report an accident or near miss is a violation of safety policy. 10. CHEMICAL AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS Only authorized personnel may handle cleaning chemicals, toners, or solvents. Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) are available at the Maintenance Office. Use chemicals only in well ventilated areas. Do not mix cleaning products (e.g., bleach and ammonia creates toxic gas). Dispose of hazardous waste (used batteries, empty chemical containers) in designated red bins. 11. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte DATA PRIVACY PRIMER FOR INTERNS Document Code: PCMC-DP-PRIMER-2026-001 Effective Date: May 1, 2026 Version: 1.0 Issued by: Compliance Office 1. PURPOSE This primer explains the basic data privacy rules that all interns must follow while assigned at Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC). It supplements Memorandum No. 21 (Series of 2026) on Data Privacy and Confidentiality. 2. WHAT IS PERSONAL DATA? Personal data means any information that can identify a person, such as: Name, address, contact number, email address Birthday, age, gender, civil status Government IDs (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, driver's license) Bank account or payroll details Attendance records and performance evaluations Sensitive personal data includes health information, biometrics, and any data about a person's race, religion, or criminal history. Interns must handle sensitive data with extra care. 3. INTERN'S RESPONSIBILITIES As an intern, you must: Keep confidential all member, employee, and cooperative data that you access during your internship. Not share any personal data with unauthorized persons (friends, family, other interns, or outside parties). Not take photos, screenshots, or photocopies of documents containing personal data unless required by your supervisor. Not post or discuss any personnel or member information on social media, messaging apps, or any public platform. Report any accidental viewing or loss of data to your supervisor and the HR Unit within 24 hours. Return all documents, access cards, and USB drives containing data at the end of your internship. 4. DATA PRIVACY RULES IN YOUR DAILY TASKS Task Encoding member information Allowed Use the coop's computer and secure database Not Allowed Bring data home or save to personal USB Task Assisting in HR records Allowed Access only files assigned by your supervisor Not Allowed Browse other employees' files Task Answering phone inquiries Allowed Verify caller identity first Not Allowed Disclose member details without consent Task Cleaning up files Allowed Shred unnecessary documents in the HR shredder bin Not Allowed Throw documents with personal data into regular trash 5. WHAT IS A DATA BREACH? A data breach happens when personal data is lost, stolen, accessed, or disclosed without authorization. Examples include: Leaving a file containing member names and addresses on a public desk. Sending an email with personal data to the wrong recipient. Losing a laptop or USB drive that contains cooperative records. An intern sharing a password to a coop system. If you suspect a breach, report it immediately to your supervisor or the Compliance Officer. Do not try to fix it alone. 6. PENALTIES FOR NON-COMPLIANCE Violation of data privacy rules may result in: First offense: Written warning and additional data privacy training. Second offense: Termination of internship plus a report to your school coordinator. If the violation is serious (e.g., intentional disclosure of sensitive data for personal gain), the cooperative may pursue legal action under the Data Privacy Act of 2012. 7. YOUR RIGHTS AS AN INTERN Under the Data Privacy Act, you have the right to: Be informed how your personal data will be used. Access your own internship records kept by the cooperative. Request correction of any inaccurate information. File a complaint with the cooperative or the National Privacy Commission if you believe your data was mishandled. The cooperative only collects your personal data for internship management, evaluation, and compliance with school requirements. 8. QUICK REMINDER CARD (FOR INTERNS) Do not share your login credentials (username and password) with anyone. Always log off from the computer before leaving your workstation. Lock physical files in the designated cabinet after use. Do not discuss intern or employee information in public areas (cafeteria, hallways). When in doubt, ask your supervisor or the Compliance Officer. 9. EMERGENCY CONTACTS FOR DATA PRIVACY CONCERNS Role Compliance Officer Name Atty. Roberto C. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte INTERNSHIP GUIDELINES (DRAFT -- 2021) Document Code: PCMC-INT-GDL-2021-DRAFT Version: 1.0 (DRAFT) Date: October 15, 2021 Prepared by: Human Resource Unit 1. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE The Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC) recognizes the value of providing meaningful internship opportunities for students from partner colleges and universities. These guidelines set forth the policies, procedures, and expectations for all interns, cooperating schools, and PCMC supervisors. These guidelines apply to all internship placements effective for Academic Year 2021--2022, subject to revision. 2. DEFINITION OF INTERNSHIP An internship is a time limited, supervised work based learning arrangement where a student (intern) performs tasks related to their academic program within PCMC. The internship is not an employment relationship. Interns receive a transportation allowance but are not entitled to employee benefits. 3. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR INTERNS To be accepted as an intern at PCMC, a student must: Be enrolled in a recognized college or university in the Philippines (preferably within Davao del Norte or Davao Region). Have completed at least 2 years (60 credit units) of their degree program. Submit a formal endorsement letter from the school's internship coordinator. Provide an updated résumé and photocopy of school ID. Pass a basic interview with the HR Department. Agree to complete a minimum of 250 internship hours (maximum 500 hours per semester). 4. INTERNSHIP PERIODS Term Summer (April – May) Preferred Duration 250 – 300 hours Application Deadline March 15 Term First Semester (June – October) Preferred Duration 300 – 400 hours Application Deadline May 30 Term Second Semester (November – March) Preferred Duration 300 – 400 hours Application Deadline October 15 Interns may request a specific schedule, subject to department needs. 5. APPLICATION PROCEDURE Step 1 – Student submits endorsement letter, résumé, and school ID to PCMC HR Unit (email: hr@panabomultipurpose.coop or walk in at HR Office). Step 2 – HR screens documents and schedules an interview (within 5 working days). Step 3 – If accepted, HR issues an Internship Offer Letter. Student must sign and return within 3 days. Step 4 – Student attends pre internship orientation and submits accomplished Intern Information Sheet, Code of Conduct acknowledgment, and Data Privacy acknowledgment. Step 5 – Student is assigned to a department and supervisor. 6. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 6.1 Intern’s Responsibilities Observe all PCMC policies, including punctuality, dress code, confidentiality, and safety rules. Complete assigned tasks diligently. Submit Weekly Accomplishment Report every Friday to supervisor and HR. Record daily attendance via DTR (biometrics or log sheet). Report any accident or incident immediately to supervisor. Return all PCMC property (ID, keys, uniform, access card) upon completion. 6.2 Supervisor’s Responsibilities Provide a meaningful work plan and orientation to departmental procedures. Monitor intern’s attendance and performance. Conduct monthly evaluation using the standard Intern Evaluation Form. Prepare final evaluation report at the end of internship. Notify HR immediately of any serious misconduct or safety issue. 6.3 HR Unit’s Responsibilities Screen and endorse applicants. Conduct general orientation for all new interns. Maintain intern records (Information Sheet, DTR, Accomplishment Reports, evaluations). Issue Certificate of Completion only after all requirements are met. 6.4 School’s Responsibilities (Partner Institution) Endorse only qualified students. Provide internship agreement signed by school representative. Assign a faculty coordinator who can be contacted by PCMC. Evaluate the student’s performance as part of academic grading. 7. ATTENDANCE AND LEAVE Official working hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (lunch break 12:00 NN – 1:00 PM). Tardiness beyond 15 minutes must be explained in writing. Three unexcused lates = one unexcused absence. Unexcused absences exceeding 10% of total internship hours may result in termination of internship. Interns may request emergency leave without pay for illness or urgent family matters. Request must be submitted to supervisor and HR at least 1 hour before shift (or as soon as possible). Make up hours may be allowed subject to supervisor’s approval. 8. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS Document Internship Agreement (signed by coop, school, student) Submitted by Student + School Deadline Day 1 of internship Document Intern Information Sheet Submitted by Student Deadline Day 1 Document Code of Conduct Acknowledgment Submitted by Student Deadline Day 1 Document Data Privacy Primer Acknowledgment Submitted by Student Deadline Day 1 Document Weekly Accomplishment Report Submitted by Student Deadline Every Friday Document Intern Evaluation Form (monthly) Submitted by Supervisor Deadline Last day of each month Document Final Report / Reflection Paper Submitted by Student Deadline Last day of internship Document Clearance Form Submitted by Student + Supervisor + HR Deadline Last day of internship Document Certificate of Completion Submitted by HR (issued) Deadline After clearance 9. EVALUATION AND GRADING Interns receive a performance rating from PCMC using the following scale: Rating 5 – Excellent Description Exceeds expectations Equivalent Grade for school reference 1.0 – 1.25 Rating 4 – Very Satisfactory Description Consistently meets Equivalent Grade for school reference 1.5 – 1.75 Rating 3 – Satisfactory Description Meets minimum Equivalent Grade for school reference 2.0 – 2.25 Rating 2 – Needs Improvement Description Below standard Equivalent Grade for school reference 2.5 – 3.0 Rating 1 – Unsatisfactory Description Fails to meet Equivalent Grade for school reference 5.0 (Fail) The final evaluation is based on attendance, quality of work, attitude, and compliance with internship guidelines. 10. Use of cooperative equipment (computers, phones, etc.) is allowed only for internship related tasks. Personal calls and use of social media during work hours are discouraged. Interns may not handle cash, sign financial documents, or access confidential member data without direct supervision. Violations may result in immediate termination of internship and a report to the school. 11. INTERNSHIP ALLOWANCE As of this draft (2021), interns receive a transportation allowance of Php 70.00 per attended day. Allowance may be adjusted based on cooperative policy. Allowance is released every 15th and 30th of the month. 12. COMPLETION AND CERTIFICATE An intern is considered complete when: Total required internship hours are logged and verified. PURPOSE This Memorandum establishes the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) for all users of Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative's (PCMC) internet connection, computer systems, email, and network resources. The policy ensures security, productivity, and compliance with applicable laws. 2. SCOPE This policy applies to all employees (regular, probationary, casual, project based), interns, contractors, and any other personnel who access PCMC's internet or network, whether using cooperative owned equipment or personal devices connected to the cooperative's network. 3. ALLOWED USE 3.1 Internet and network resources are provided primarily for work related activities, including: Research and tasks related to assigned duties Communication with members, partner institutions, and government agencies Access to cooperative approved software and cloud services Training and professional development (with supervisor approval) 3.2 Limited personal use during breaks (lunch hour or official rest periods) is permitted provided it does not: Violate any law or cooperative policy Consume excessive bandwidth Interfere with work productivity 4. PROHIBITED ACTIVITIES The following are strictly prohibited: Accessing, downloading, or distributing pornographic, obscene, or sexually explicit material. Engaging in illegal activities (e.g., hacking, piracy, unauthorized access to other systems). Sending harassing, threatening, or discriminatory messages via email or chat. Using the network for personal business or commercial ventures. Installing unauthorized software or hardware on cooperative computers. Bypassing security controls (firewalls, content filters, proxy settings). Streaming video or music for entertainment purposes during work hours (except for work related training). Online gambling or accessing gaming sites. Knowingly introducing malware, viruses, or ransomware into the network. 5. INTERNET SECURITY AND CONFIDENTIALITY 5.1 Users must protect their login credentials and not share passwords. 5.2 Do not send unencrypted sensitive or confidential information (member data, personnel records) over email unless authorized. 5.3 Report any suspected security breach (unusual network activity, phishing emails) to the IT Support Unit immediately. 5.4 All devices connected to the PCMC network must have updated antivirus software. Personal devices must be scanned before connection. 6. MONITORING AND PRIVACY PCMC reserves the right to monitor internet usage, email communications, and network activity to ensure compliance with this policy. Users have no reasonable expectation of privacy when using cooperative resources. Monitoring methods include: Web content filtering logs Bandwidth usage reports Email filtering systems Periodic audits of browsing history 7. VIOLATIONS AND PENALTIES Offense Minor (e.g., excessive personal browsing, streaming) Employee Written warning Intern Verbal warning plus reminder Offense Moderate (e.g., installing unapproved software, sharing password) Employee 3 day suspension Intern Written warning plus conference with school Offense Severe (e.g., accessing pornographic or illegal sites, hacking, data theft) Employee Termination Intern Immediate termination plus report to school and legal authorities All violations shall be documented and placed in the personnel or intern file. 8. INTERNET USAGE GUIDELINES FOR INTERNS Interns must obtain permission from their supervisor before downloading large files or accessing external cloud storage. Personal devices (laptops, phones) may only connect to the guest Wi Fi, not the internal network, unless authorized by IT. Interns who violate this policy may lose internet access privileges in addition to disciplinary action. 9. EXCEPTION REQUESTS Any user who requires access to a website or service normally blocked for legitimate work purposes must submit a written request to the IT Support Unit and HR Manager. extracted_text: Title Slide Data Privacy Basics for HR Personnel Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative (PCMC) Human Resource Unit [PCMC Logo] Trainer: Compliance Officer / HR Manager Date: [Training Date] Version: FINAL FINAL Slide 2 – Training Objectives By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Understand key concepts of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (R.A. 10173) Identify personal and sensitive personal information in HR context Apply proper handling, storage, and disposal of personnel and intern records Recognize and report a data breach Comply with PCMC's Data Privacy Policy (Memorandum No. 21, Series 2026) Slide 3 – Agenda 1. Why Data Privacy Matters for PCMC 2. Legal Framework: Data Privacy Act of 2012 3. Types of Data: Personal vs. Sensitive Personal 4. HR Data Lifecycle (Collection, Use, Storage, Disposal) 5. Rights of Data Subjects (Employees and Interns) 6. Security Measures (Physical, Technical, Administrative) 7. Data Breach: Definition, Examples, and Reporting 8. PCMC-Specific Rules (from Memo No. 21) 9. Penalties for Non-Compliance 10. Case Studies and Q&A Slide 4 – Why Data Privacy Matters for PCMC We handle personal data of 15,000+ members, 120 employees, and 20+ interns per batch Trust is our currency – members rely on us to protect their information Violations lead to: Legal liability (fines up to PHP 5M + imprisonment) Damage to cooperative's reputation Loss of member confidence Disciplinary action for employees/interns Slide 5 – Legal Framework: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (R.A. 10173) Purpose: Protect personal information in government and private sector Applies to: Any person or entity processing personal data Key principles: Transparency, legitimate purpose, proportionality NPC: National Privacy Commission – overseeing compliance PCMC is a personal information controller – responsible for ensuring data privacy. Slide 6 – Types of Data Personal Information Name, address, contact number, email Gender, age, civil status School, course, year level SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG numbers (some considered sensitive under certain context) Sensitive Personal Information Race, ethnicity, religion Health records, biometrics Criminal history Trade union membership Rule: Sensitive data requires higher level of protection and explicit consent. Slide 7 – HR Data Lifecycle Collection Only collect what is necessary for internship/employment Obtain signed consent (via Intern Information Sheet, Employment Form) Use Use data only for intended purpose (e.g., payroll, evaluation, school reporting) Storage Physical files: Locked cabinets, restricted access Digital files: Password-protected, encrypted, access logs Disposal Shred physical documents after retention period (5 years for employees, 2 years for interns) Securely delete digital files (not just recycle bin) Slide 8 – Rights of Data Subjects (Employees and Interns) Under the Data Privacy Act, individuals have the right to: 1. Be informed – how their data will be used 2. Access – request copy of their records 3. Rectification – correct inaccurate data 4. Erasure or blocking – request removal under certain conditions 5. Object to processing 6. Data portability – transfer data to another entity 7. File a complaint with NPC HR must respond to access/rectification requests within 15 working days. Slide 9 – Security Measures at PCMC Physical Security HR filing cabinet with lock – key only with HR Manager and designated staff Visitor log for HR office Shredder for disposal Technical Security Password-protected computers (change every 90 days) Anti-virus and firewall Encrypted USB drives if used Administrative Security Signed confidentiality agreements (all employees and interns) Regular data privacy training Limited access based on role Slide 10 – What is a Data Breach? A data breach occurs when personal data is accessed, disclosed, or lost without authorization. Examples in HR context: Leaving a personnel file on an office desk overnight Email containing member list sent to wrong recipient Lost laptop with unencrypted HR records Intern sharing password to a coop system Discarding documents with personal data in regular trash Slide 11 – Breach Reporting Protocol (PCMC Memo No. 21) Within 24 hours of discovery: 1. Immediately report to Compliance Officer (Atty. Roberto C. Fernandez) and HR Manager 2. Do not attempt to fix or delete evidence alone 3. Secure affected area or devices 4. HR and Compliance will assess if breach is notifiable to NPC and affected individuals Failure to report = serious violation (possible termination). Slide 12 – PCMC-Specific Rules (From Memo No. 21 – Privacy Update) All personnel and interns must sign revised Privacy Acknowledgment Form Only authorized HR and Compliance personnel may access personnel files Third-party requests require written approval from Compliance Office Retention: Employee records – 5 years after separation; Intern records – 2 years Breach notification to NPC within 72 hours if required Slide 13 – Penalties for Non-Compliance Under Data Privacy Act (R.A. 10173): Unauthorized processing: PHP 1M – 5M fine + imprisonment (1-3 years) Unauthorized disclosure: PHP 1M – 5M fine + imprisonment (1-5 years) Unauthorized access: PHP 500K – 2M fine + imprisonment (6 months – 2 years) Internal PCMC penalties (for employees/interns): First offense: Written warning + retraining Second offense: Suspension (employees) / termination (interns) Severe violation (intentional breach): Immediate termination + legal action Slide 14 – Case Studies (Group Discussion) Case 1: An HR staff member receives an email requesting a copy of an intern's evaluation form from the intern's friend (not authorized). What should the staff do? Answer: Deny access, verify identity, refer to supervisor. Case 2: An intern accidentally leaves a printed DTR containing names and attendance of 10 interns in the cafeteria. Another employee finds it. What steps must be taken? Answer: Report to HR within 1 hour, secure document, document incident, notify affected interns. Case 3: The HR Manager needs to send a list of employees with their birthdates to the cooperative's events committee for a birthday fund. Is this allowed? Answer: Yes, if limited to necessary data (name + birthdate) and recipients are authorized. Slide 15 – Quick Reminders for HR Personnel Always log off when leaving your workstation Do not discuss personnel matters in public areas (cafeteria, hallways, elevators) Never share your login credentials – not even with colleagues When in doubt about sharing data, ask the Compliance Officer Report any suspected breach immediately – no penalty for good faith reporting Slide 16 – Training Acknowledgment All participants must sign the Data Privacy Training Acknowledgment Sheet before leaving. The signed sheet confirms that you: Attended the complete training Understood your responsibilities under R.A. 10173 and PCMC policies Agree to comply with all data privacy rules Slide 17 – Q&A and Contact Information Questions? Compliance Officer: Atty. Roberto C. Fernandez – local 205 / 0917-999-8888 HR Manager: Maria L. Santos – local 108 / 0917-777-8888 Email for privacy concerns: privacy@panabomultipurpose.coop National Privacy Commission (NPC): www.privacy.gov.ph | Hotline (02) 8823-9290 Slide 18 – Closing Slide Thank you for protecting our members' and personnel's privacy! 'Privacy is not an option – it is a responsibility.' Panabo City Multipurpose Cooperative – Human Resource Unit

Santos, HR Manager DATE: October 1, 2026 SUBJECT: Visitor Handling Protocol (Version 2.0) – Updated for 2026 In line with the Cooperative's commitment to security, professionalism, and member service, the following Visitor Handling Protocol is hereby revised and takes effect immediately. This version (v2) supersedes all previous visitor guidelines. All personnel, security guards, and interns must strictly observe the procedures below. I. PURPOSE To ensure that all visitors (members, guests, suppliers, government officials, walk in clients) are received, identified, and assisted in a safe, courteous, and efficient manner while protecting cooperative assets and confidentiality. II. DEFINITION OF VISITOR For this protocol, a 'visitor' refers to any person who is not a regular employee or currently assigned intern of PCMC, including: Cooperative members transacting at the counter Deliveries and suppliers Guests of employees/interns (with prior approval) Government or CDA representatives Job applicants / walk in interviewees Students inquiring about internships III. GENERAL RULES – ALL VISITORS 1. All visitors must report to the Reception / Security Desk at the main entrance. 2. Present a valid government issued ID (e.g., PhilID, driver's license, passport, UMID). For members, PCMC Member ID is acceptable. 3. Sign the Visitor Logbook indicating: name, time in, time out, purpose, and person to visit. 4. Receive a Visitor ID / Pass which must be visibly worn at all times inside the premises. 5. Visitors without valid ID shall be accompanied by an employee/intern at all times. 6. Return the Visitor ID and log out upon departure. IV. SPECIFIC GUIDELINES BY VISITOR TYPE Visitor Type Cooperative member (transaction) Procedure Proceed directly to Member Services counter – no need for Visitor ID if staying in lobby Allowed Areas Ground Floor lobby, Member Services area Escort Required? No Visitor Type Member (meeting with staff/manager) Procedure Security calls concerned employee. Visitor signs log and wears Visitor ID. Allowed Areas Assigned office only Escort Required? Yes, by the employee Visitor Type Supplier / delivery personnel Procedure Report to Security Desk. Delivery items to be inspected. Visitor ID issued. Remain at Receiving Area unless escorted. Allowed Areas Receiving Area only Escort Required? Yes, to other offices Visitor Type Government / CDA representative Procedure HR / Compliance notified immediately. Visitor logs, wears ID. Escorted to meeting room. Allowed Areas Designated meeting room Escort Required? Yes (HR or Compliance staff) Visitor Type Job applicant / interviewee Procedure Proceed to HR Unit. Visitor ID issued. Wait at HR waiting area. Allowed Areas HR Unit waiting area Escort Required? No, but stay in HR area Visitor Type Guest of employee/intern Procedure Prior written or phone approval from department head required. Log in, wear ID. Escorted by the employee/intern. Allowed Areas Only the employee's assigned office / cubicle Escort Required? Yes, at all times Visitor Type Student inquiring about internship Procedure Refer to HR Unit. Visitor ID issued. Wait at HR waiting area. Allowed Areas HR Unit waiting area Escort Required? No V. PROHIBITED ACTIONS FOR VISITORS Visitors are not allowed to: Enter restricted areas (e.g., Cash Vault, IT Server Room, HR Records Room, Board Room unless authorized) Take photographs or videos inside the cooperative without prior written permission from the General Manager Use cooperative computers, phones, or Wi Fi unless explicitly authorized by the host employee Loiter in corridors or break areas Smoke anywhere inside the building (designated smoking area outside only) Any violation may result in the visitor being asked to leave and blacklisting from future visits. VI. RESPONSIBILITIES OF EMPLOYEES AND INTERNS Employees expecting a visitor must inform the Security Desk at least 15 minutes before arrival (via telephone or email to security@panabomultipurpose.coop). Meet your visitor at the Reception / Security Desk – do not ask the visitor to wander inside to find you. Escort your visitor at all times, including to the restroom if necessary. Sign the Visitor Logbook as 'host' upon your visitor's departure. Report any suspicious behavior immediately to Security or HR. Interns may not receive personal visitors unless approved by their supervisor. VII. EMERGENCY VISITORS (Media, Law Enforcement, Medical) Law enforcement (police, NBI, etc.) – Immediately notify the Compliance Officer and General Manager. Require presentation of official ID and mission order before allowing entry. Escort to a private meeting room. Media – Refer to the General Manager's Office. No employee or intern shall speak to media without authorization. Medical emergency (ambulance, paramedics) – Allow immediate access to the affected area. Security shall accompany. Notify HR within 5 minutes. VIII. MONITORING AND COMPLIANCE Security personnel shall maintain the Visitor Logbook and submit a weekly summary to HR. CCTV footage covering entrances, lobby, and corridors shall be retained for 30 days. HR and Security shall conduct random spot checks on Visitor ID compliance. IX. PENALTIES FOR NON COMPLIANCE (Employees / Interns) Violation Failure to escort visitor 1st Offense Written warning 2nd Offense 1 day suspension 3rd Offense 3 day suspension Violation Allowing visitor in restricted area 1st Offense Written warning + retraining 2nd Offense 3 day suspension 3rd Offense Termination Violation Forging visitor signature or log 1st Offense Immediate suspension pending investigation 2nd Offense – 3rd Offense – Violation Visitor related incident not reported 1st Offense Written warning 2nd Offense Written reprimand 3rd Offense 5 day suspension Visitors who violate rules will be asked to leave. Repeated violations by the same visitor may result in blacklisting from PCMC premises. X. ATTACHMENTS Annex A: Visitor Logbook (template) Annex B: Visitor ID / Pass (design) Annex C: Escort Protocol for Restricted Areas XI. EFFECTIVITY This Memorandum (No. 32, Series of 2026, Rev. 2) takes effect on October 1, 2026. All previous visitor handling guidelines are hereby revoked. PANABO CITY MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE Panabo City, Davao del Norte MEMORANDUM NO. 41 Series of 2021 TO: All Employees, Interns, and IT Users FROM: Maria L. Santos, HR Manager DATE: August 16, 2021 SUBJECT: Notice on Unauthorized File Sharing and Use of External Storage Devices In line with the Cooperative's commitment to data security, confidentiality, and compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012, all personnel and interns are hereby reminded of the strict prohibition against unauthorized file sharing and the use of unapproved external storage devices. Recent monitoring has revealed instances of employees transferring cooperative documents to personal USB drives and sharing internal files via personal email and unsecured cloud services. Such actions pose serious risks to the Cooperative's sensitive information, member data, and intellectual property. I. PROHIBITED ACTIONS The following are strictly prohibited effective immediately: Copying or transferring any cooperative-related file (member lists, financial reports, HR records, internal memos, etc.) to personal USB drives, external hard drives, or personal cloud storage (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) without explicit written authorization from the Department Head and IT Support. Sending cooperative files through personal email accounts (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.) instead of the official PCMC email system. Using third-party file-sharing applications (e.g., WeTransfer, Telegram, WhatsApp) to share work documents. Sharing login credentials to cooperative systems or network drives with anyone not authorized. Printing or photocopying confidential documents for off-site use without clearance. II. ALLOWED METHODS FOR FILE SHARING Internal network shared drive (\PCMC-Server\Departments) for department use. Official PCMC email (@panabomultipurpose.coop) with encryption for sensitive attachments. Approved USB drives issued by IT Support (logged and tracked) – only for legitimate work purposes and returned after use. Interns may only receive files via official email or direct transfer from their supervisor. III. RESPONSIBILITIES OF EMPLOYEES AND INTERNS Employees shall not bypass security controls. Any work-related file transfer outside the approved methods must be requested in writing to IT and HR. Interns are not permitted to bring or use personal USB drives. Interns who need to transfer files for school requirements must have their supervisor's written approval and use an IT-issued encrypted drive. All users must report any suspected unauthorized file sharing immediately to IT Support or the Compliance Officer. IV. CONSEQUENCES OF VIOLATION Any violation of this policy shall be subject to disciplinary action as follows: Offense First offense (minor – e.g., using personal USB once without authorization) Employee Written warning + mandatory data security retraining Intern Written warning + conference with school coordinator Offense Second offense (repeated unauthorized transfer) Employee 5 day suspension Intern Immediate termination of internship + report to school Offense Third offense or intentional sharing of confidential data (e.g., member list, financials) Employee Termination of employment Intern Same as above + possible legal action In addition, the Cooperative reserves the right to file criminal or civil charges under the Data Privacy Act (R.A. 10173) and other applicable laws for serious breaches. V. EXCEPTIONS Requests for legitimate file sharing outside the allowed methods must be submitted using the Request for External File Transfer Form (available at IT Office). Approval must be obtained before any transfer. VI. EFFECTIVITY This Memorandum takes effect immediately upon issuance and supersedes any prior inconsistent notices. For questions, please contact IT Support at local 401 or HR Unit at local 108. Strict compliance is required. MARIA L. SANTOS HR Manager Noted by: ROBERTO V. TAN General Manager Conformed by: Leo C.
